questions.stem: On which issue does India stand to benefit from its relationship with Russia?
options: Cold War alliance to power blocs.
As part of SAARC as founding members.
In establishing a stable democracy in Pakistan and Bangladesh.

match.front: Which region does India gain access to through its relationship with Russia?
match.back:
Central Asia
access to Central Asia, and balancing its relations with China.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 1, page 13

questions.stem: In which one of the following steel plants did Russia not give aid and assistance to India?

match.front: For which steel plants did the USSR give India aid and technical assistance?
match.back: It gave aid and technical assistance for steel plants like Bhilai, Bokaro, Visakhapatnam, and machinery plants like Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd., etc.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 1, page 12

questions.stem:
Which of the following were the consequences of shock therapy administered in post-communist regimes?

(C) Privatisation led to reduction of disparities between rich and poor regions.
(D) The withdrawal of government subsidies pushed large sections of the people into poverty.

match.front: Why did many people in post-communist states lose all their savings under shock therapy?
match.back:
Because the rate of inflation was very high
The rate of inflation was so high that people lost all their savings.

questions.stem: The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) was established in ________ by five countries of this by signing the ________ Declaration.

match.front: When and how was ASEAN established, and by which five countries?
match.back: ASEAN was established in 1967 by five countries of this region — Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand — by signing the Bangkok Declaration.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 2, page 20

Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited China in 2017.
Chinese President Xi Jinping paid a visit to India in 2018.

match.back: A series of talks to resolve the border issue were also initiated in 1981.

match.front: Why was the Congress all-inclusive in nature?

match.front: Why did the Socialists form a separate Socialist Party in 1948?

match.source: NCERT, Politics in India since Independence, chapter 2, page 34

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are correct about resistance to globalisation?
(A) Anti-globalisation movements participate in global networks.
(B) The 1999 World Trade Organisation (WTO) Ministerial Meeting in Seattle witnessed widespread protests.
(C) The World Social Forum (WSF) is a global platform opposed to neo-liberal globalisation.
(D) In February 2024, the WSF meeting was held in Porto Alegre, Brazil.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

match.front: Where was the World Social Forum (WSF) meeting held in February 2024?
match.back:
In Nepal
The latest WSF meeting was held in Nepal in February 2024.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 7, page 111

questions.stem: Those who argue that there is something distinct about contemporary globalisation, point out to which one of the following?
options: Globalisation has taken place through much of human history.
It is a mistake to assume globalisation as a purely cultural phenomenon.
The vastly uneven impact of globalisation on the Global North.
Scale and speed of flows account for the uniqueness of globalisation.

match.front: What makes contemporary globalisation unique, according to those who see it as distinct?
match.back: those who argue that there is something distinct about contemporary globalisation point out that it is the scale and speed of these flows that account for the uniqueness of globalisation in the contemporary era.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 7, page 102

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not correct regarding the political consequence of globalisation?
options: 'Minimalist state' is giving way to a more 'welfare state'.
The state continues to discharge essential functions of law and order and national security.
Market becomes the prime determinant of economic and social priorities.
Increased role of multinational companies lead to reduction in decision-making capacity of government.

match.front: All over the world, the old `welfare state' is now giving way to a more ____.
match.back: All over the world, the old `welfare state' is now giving way to a more minimalist state.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 7, page 103

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements are related to the First Five Year Plan (1951-1956)?
(A) Huge allocations were made for the Bhakhra Nangal Dam.
(B) It identified the pattern of land distribution in the country.
(C) It imposed substantial tariffs on imports.
(D) It sought to push savings up.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

match.front: In the First Five Year Plan, what did the planners seek to do about the savings of the people?
match.back:
They sought to push savings up
So the planners sought to push savings up.
match.source: NCERT, Politics in India since Independence, chapter 3, page 51

questions.stem: India's Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966) was criticised for which of the following?
options: Increasing the possibility of food shortage.
Spending foreign exchange to buy technology from the global market.
Attracting more investment for green revolution.

match.front: What unmistakable bias did critics point out in the Third Plan's strategies?
match.back: The Third Plan was not significantly different from the Second. Critics pointed out that the plan strategies from this time around displayed an unmistakable “urban bias”.
match.source: NCERT, Politics in India since Independence, chapter 3, page 52

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements does not capture the essence of 'cooperative security'?
options: Cooperation may be bilateral, regional, continental, or global.
It involves non-governmental organisations, businesses and corporations, and great personalities.
It may involve the use of force as the first choice.
It depends on the nature of the threat and the willingness and ability of countries to respond.

match.front: When may cooperative security involve the use of force?
match.back: Cooperative security may involve the use of force as a last resort.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 5, page 76

questions.stem:
Arrange the following landmark events in the correct chronological order.
(A) India's first nuclear explosion
(B) Chemical Weapons Convention
(C) Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
(D) Anti-ballistic Missile Treaty
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

match.front: What did the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) of 1968 regulate?
match.back: The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) of 1968 was an arms control treaty in the sense that it regulated the acquisition of nuclear weapons: those countries that had tested and manufactured nuclear weapons before 1967 were allowed to keep their weapons; and those that had not done so were to give up the right to acquire them.
match.source: NCERT, Contemporary World Politics, chapter 5, page 69

questions.stem:
What were the challenges faced by independent India?
(A) Shape a nation that was united, yet accommodative of the diversity of Indian society.
(B) Develop democratic practices in accordance with the Constitution.
(C) Divide the administrative apparatus and financial assets and liabilities after partition.
(D) Ensure the development and well-being of the entire society.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

match.front: What was the first and immediate challenge faced by independent India?
match.back: The first and the immediate challenge was to shape a nation that was united, yet accommodative of the diversity in our society.
match.source: NCERT, Politics in India since Independence, chapter 1, page 4

questions.stem: The intergation of Princely States in India after independence involved which one of the following?
options: The issue of Hyderabad was resolved after a plebiscite confirmed people's desire to join India.
Razakars, a para-military force, was unleashed on the people of Junagarh.
Maharaja of Manipur signed the Instrument of Accession with the Indian government on assurance of internal autonomy.
Mahatma Gandhi played a historic role in negotiating with the rulers of princely states.

match.front: Who was the Maharaja of Manipur who signed the Instrument of Accession?
match.back: A few days before Independence, the Maharaja of Manipur, Bodhachandra Singh, signed the Instrument of Accession with the Indian government on the assurance that the internal autonomy of Manipur would be maintained.
match.source: NCERT, Politics in India since Independence, chapter 1, page 18

questions.stem: Which cities became divided into 'communal zones' as a consequence of partition?

match.back:
Amritsar and Kolkata (with Lahore)
Amritsar and Kolkata became divided into ‘communal zones’.

questions.stem: Dalit Shoshit Samaj Sangharsh Samiti emerged under the leadership of-

questions.stem: Which one of the following statement is correct about 2014 elections?
options: BJP won 300 seats on its own.
BJP became the first party to gain single party majority after 30 years.
BJP chose to form NDA government without any coalition partner.
For 2014 elections, BJP declared its Prime Ministerial candidate in 2012.

match.front: How many seats did the BJP win on its own in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections?
match.back: BJP under the leadership of Narendra Modi got a clear majority in 16th Lok Sabha elections held in 2014. BJP won 282 seats on its own, becoming the first party to gain single party majority after 30 years.
match.source: NCERT, Politics in India since Independence, chapter 8, page 152

questions.stem: India's foreign policy from 1946 to 1964 did not involve-
options: Protesting against Britain's attack on Egypt over the Suez Canal issue in 1956.
Publically condemning USSR's invasion of Hungary in 1956.
Keeping away from the US-led North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
Keeping away from the Soviet-led Warsaw Pact.

match.front: How did India respond in 1956 to the Suez Canal attack on Egypt and to the Soviet invasion of Hungary?
match.back: In 1956 when Britain attacked Egypt over the Suez Canal issue, India led the world protest against this neo-colonial invasion. But in the same year when the USSR invaded Hungary, India did not join its public condemnation.
match.source: NCERT, Politics in India since Independence, chapter 4, page 57

questions.stem: The split in the Congress in 1969 was projected by Indira Gandhi as-

Ensuring that the smaller factions within the Congress do away with the differences.
An ideological divide between socialists and conservatives.

match.chapter: Challenges to & Restoration of the Congress System
match.front: How did Indira Gandhi project the 1969 split?

questions.stem: The regional aspiration of Jammu and Kashmir after independence is related to-

questions.stem: What was the consensus built on the question of development in the first decade of independence?

match.back: Despite the various differences, there was a consensus on one point: that development could not be left to private actors, that there was the need for the government to develop a design or plan for development.
